Guidance & outlook: We are quite confident that FY25-26 will be a very robust year.
It is a very healthy growth and PBT of Q1FY25-26 is Rs.
Q2 also is looking good, and therefore, we are quite hopeful that we will have a strong FY25-26.
Growth & demand: All the tax related issues have been taken care of , and therefore, we are now sort of ready to embark on a growth path as we were several years back before we had this downturn.
We have also sort of expanded with semiconductor growth happening.
Sir, these new segments, which are opening up, like EVs, semiconductors, drones, we have an opportunity to launch newer magazines to cover these areas because they are in great demand today.
Margins & costs: Investment rationale for the rights issue, we have taken care of legacy issues, obviously those legacy issues cost us some money.
Capex & expansion: There are f ive key pillars, one is digital first solutions, second is innovation on products and content, third is geographical expansion, and the fourth is diversified revenue streams and operational efficiency.
Balance sheet & cash: 3.31 crore to meet the working capital requirement , and Rs.
Risks & challenges: The Company went through a lot of problems and primarily these problems came because of our US business challenges.
Our US business challenges have been resolved and the business has been closed.
When one has so many things happening around oneself, then obviously there is pressure on the core business.

Guidance & outlook: Media Industry Business Overview India's Entertainment & Media industry is expected to reach INR 4,30,401 crore by 2026, growing at an 8.8% CAGR, positioning the country as one of the fastest-growing E&M markets globally.
Meanwhile, the digital advertising segment's 12.1% CAGR reflects a structural shift in advertiser preferences toward targeted, data-driven digital formats.

The OTT video segment is set to expand at a 14.1% CAGR to reach INR 21,032 crore in 2026, with subscription services accounting for 90.5% of revenue in 2021 and expected to reach 95% by 2026, further accelerating the migration of both audiences and advertiser budgets toward digital platforms.
Growth & demand: India will be the only country in the world to grow daily print newspaper & magazine copy sales by volume during the forecast period at a 1.3% CAGR, reaching an average of 139 million daily print newspaper sales in 2026, one-third of the global daily total, which will mean India overtakes China as the biggest world market for print edition readership in 2025…
The Company is happy to report that in FY2025-26 has regained its growth, crossing the INR 100 Crore revenue mark.
This represents a YoY growth of 19.32% on topline revenue, and a 711.97% growth in EBITDA.
Margins & costs: In FY 2025-26, the CMIL registered revenue of INR 104.59 Crore, with an EBITDA of INR 6.72 Crore, and a PBT of INR 4.85 Crore.
Furthermore, Q4, FY 2025-26 recorded revenue of INR 28.48 Crore with an EBITDA of INR 1.93 Crore.
Cost comprises all cost of purchase, cost of conversion and other costs incurred in bringing the inventories to their present location and condition.
